question: Violence against women continues to be a serious problem across all EU Member States. However, comparable, reliable data on the extent and forms of gender-based violence against women in the EU remain limited1.

The lack of harmonised recording methods and the different definitions used in the various Member States make it hard to provide an accurate picture of the true extent of the phenomenon, which in turn makes effective prevention and response difficult. It is essential to develop integrated data systems in the EU that make it possible to identify the problem and take targeted measures.

Taking into account: Article 11 of the Istanbul Convention, which obliges states to collect disaggregated relevant statistical data on cases of all forms of violence covered by the scope of the Convention2; Article 44 of the Directive on combating violence against women and domestic violence, which makes it compulsory for comprehensive and comparable disaggregated data to be collected and transmitted to the European Union3; and the fact that the President of the Commission has tasked Commissioner-designate Hadja Lahbib with improving the collection of comparable data in the European Union4, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
How does it plan to ensure the systematic and effective collection of comparable data by Member States with a view to addressing gender-based violence?
Does it intend to adopt specific guidelines or a single framework for the collection of this data, based on the EIGE’s recommendations and the provisions of the relevant directive?

For an overview of national indicators and definitions please visit the EIGE website: https://eige.europa.eu/gender-based-violence/data-collection. The European Union acceded to the Istanbul Convention on 28 June 2023. For more information see https://rm.coe.int/168008482e.

Member States are required to develop standardised data in cooperation with the EIGE and to transmit them to the Commission (Eurostat) https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=OJ:L_202401385. For more information, see the mission letter addressed by President von der Leyen to Commissionerdesignate Hadja Lahbib https://commission.europa.eu/document/download/faaf33ff-c8c7-49a1-b01d56681e11a5e6_en?
filename=Mission%20letter%20-%20LAHBIB.pdf.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (25.3.2025) In accordance with Article 44 of Directive 2024/13851, Member States are required to disaggregate data by sex, age group of the victim and the offender (child/adult), type of offence and the relationship between the victim and the offender.

As a minimum, Member States are required to collect statistics on annual numbers of reported offences and convictions of violence against women and/or domestic violence; the number of victims who have been killed; the number and capacity of shelters per Member State, as well as the number of calls to national helplines.

The European Institute for Gender Equality will continue supporting Member States, including by establishing common standards for the collection of administrative data. The Commission is assisting Member States in the correct implementation of the Directive and its provisions, including the aforementioned data collection requirement.

Directive 2024/1385 also requires Member States – in line with the Istanbul Convention – to endeavour to conduct population-based surveys at regular intervals to assess the prevalence of and trends in all forms of violence covered by the Directive. In 2020, Eurostat developed a common questionnaire and methodology for the EU gender-based violence survey.
The indicators, as well as the aggregated results of this survey with data for all Member States and the EU average are publicly available on the Eurostat website.

2 The Commission relies on the Member States to cooperate with Eurostat to produce regular, high quality and comparable data on gender-based violence in the future, as well as use this methodological manual developed by Eurostat to conduct their own population-based surveys.
1 To be transposed by June 2027. 2 EU gender-based violence survey 2024, Eurostat, https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/products-statistical-
